newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Levy to Egypt on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Levy to Egypt on Tuesday.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy will go to Egypt on Tuesday for talks on ending a Middle East peacemaking crisis that deepened with a suicide bombing in a Jerusalem street market.

Ministry spokesman Aviv Shir-On on Sunday said Levy was invited by his Egyptian counterpart Amr Moussa for Tuesday and would apparently also meet President Hosni Mubarak. He said the meetings could take place in Alexandria.
They would discuss Middle East peacemaking, Shir-On said, adding: "Obviously with the attack and all that has to do with it, it increases the need to speak."
Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat met Mubarak in Egypt on Saturday.

Egypt, which became the first Arab state to make peace with Israel in 1979, has been trying to revive Israeli-Palestinian peace talks which collapsed when Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Days before Wednesday's attack, Levy and a negotiator for Arafat had agreed the sides would resume stalled talks on carrying out interim accords.
Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet demanded Arafat crack down on Moslem militants behind the double suicide bombing on Wednesday that killed 13 people and wounded 170.

Israel also suspended peace talks with the Palestinians, rounded up scores of suspected militants, closed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, demanded the extradition of the PLO police chief and threatened to re-enter Palestinian self-rule areas to seize militants if Arafat failed to do the job.
